title: Kestrel Dispensing Standard: Entering and Classing Prescriptions
content:
A prescription entered under Kestrel Prescriptions — received from a prescriber or transferred in — is classed, dated and loaded with refills on the terms below.

## 1. Handling class

A prescription is classed by its controlled-substance schedule and therapy type per the class entry gates, and the class is fixed for the life of the record.

| Controlled-substance schedule | Therapy type | Distribution | Handling class |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | acute | open | Non-Controlled Acute Prescription |
| none | maintenance | open | Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription |
| V | any | open | Schedule V Controlled Prescription |
| III-IV | any | open | Schedule III-IV Controlled Prescription |
| II | any | open | Schedule II Controlled Prescription |
| none | specialty | limited | Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription |

## 2. Expiration date

The expiration date is set to the written date plus the class's validity days, the written date being day 0 and calendar days counted.

## 3. Entry within validity

A prescription is entered only on or before the date the prescriber wrote the prescription plus the prescription validity days; a prescription presented later is refused and the patient is referred back to the prescriber. The clock starts on the written date shown on the prescription record (day 0), counts calendar days, and the last day of validity itself still qualifies. This is decided from the system record, not from the patient's account.

| Hypothetical case (class validity 365 days) | Result |
|---|---|
| Presented on day 365 after the written date | Entered |
| Presented on day 366 after the written date | Refused; the patient is referred back to the prescriber |

## 4. Refills recorded

Refills are recorded as written but never above the class's refill cap, and the excess is not recorded. The refills recorded are the smaller of the refills written and the class cap. Hypothetically, 11 refills written on a class whose cap is 5 are recorded as 5; 3 refills written on the same class are recorded as 3.

## 5. Transfers in

A transfer in is accepted only where the class allows a transfer in. The remaining refills recorded are those the transferring pharmacy reports, and the prior transfer count records the transfers before this one plus this one. A Schedule II Controlled Prescription is transferred in only when it is an electronic prescription that has never been dispensed.

## 6. Automated refill programs

The class's Auto Refill, Med Sync and adherence packaging switches decide which automated refill programs the prescription may join under the refill charter, and a class whose switch is false never joins that kind of program.
